methods.label: Count equally likely label pairs
methods.explanation:
Each die has three equally likely labels because each label appears on two of its six faces. Record each outcome as an ordered pair, with the even die first. There are \(3\cdot3=9\) possible label pairs, and each corresponds to \(2\cdot2=4\) of the \(36\) equally likely face pairs. Thus the nine label pairs are equally likely.

For the even labels \(2,4,6\), the only odd labels that make a sum of \(7\) are respectively \(5,3,1\). The favorable pairs are exactly
\[
(2,5),\quad (4,3),\quad (6,1).
\]
These are distinct, and every successful roll belongs to one of them. Therefore the probability is
\[
\frac{3}{9}=\boxed{\frac{1}{3}},
\]
choice D.
